questions.q: What is an AWS Availability Zone in relation to an AWS Region?
options: An AZ is a larger geographic area that contains multiple Regions
AZs and Regions refer to the same thing
A Region is a geographic area containing multiple isolated, physically separate data centers called Availability Zones
An AZ is a single physical server rack
questions.explain: AWS groups its data centers into Regions (broad geographic areas), and each Region contains multiple Availability Zones — physically separate facilities with independent power, cooling, and networking.

questions.q: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system on an EC2 instance?
options: The customer, since EC2 follows AWS's infrastructure model where the customer manages the guest OS
AWS, since it manages all patching for every EC2 instance automatically
Neither - the guest OS never needs patching
AWS Support, but only for customers on a paid support plan
questions.explain: For EC2, AWS secures the underlying hardware, hypervisor, and network, but everything above that — the guest OS, applications, and data — is the customer's responsibility, including patching.

questions.q: What is the primary benefit of using AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts?
options: It merges all member accounts into a single account
It's required before you're allowed to create more than one IAM user
It automatically encrypts all data across every member account
Centralized billing and the ability to apply policies like Service Control Policies (SCPs) across all member accounts
questions.explain: AWS Organizations lets you consolidate billing across accounts and apply Service Control Policies that set permission guardrails across every account in the organization, without merging the accounts themselves.

questions.q: Why is it a best practice to avoid using the AWS account root user for everyday tasks?
options: The root user can only view billing information and nothing else
The root user has unrestricted access to everything in the account, including billing, and its permissions can't be restricted by IAM policies
IAM users always cost extra compared to using the root user
The root user cannot sign in to the AWS Management Console
questions.explain: The root user's permissions can't be limited by IAM policies, so if its credentials are compromised the entire account — billing included — is exposed; day-to-day work should use IAM users or roles with scoped permissions instead.

questions.q: Which best describes what AWS provides to customers?
options: On-demand compute, storage, database, and other IT infrastructure services billed on a pay-as-you-go basis
A single physical data center that customers rent in full by the month
A free tier that never expires or shifts to paid billing
One all-in-one application used only for building websites
questions.explain: AWS is a cloud platform offering a broad catalog of on-demand infrastructure and managed services — compute, storage, databases, networking, and more — that customers provision as needed and pay for based on usage.

questions.q: Why do many highly available AWS architectures deploy resources across multiple Availability Zones within a Region rather than just one?
options: Using multiple AZs is required before you're allowed to create an S3 bucket
AZs within the same Region are located in different countries
Each AZ has independent power, cooling, and networking, so an outage in one AZ is unlikely to take down the others
Spreading resources across AZs is the only way AWS allows you to reduce cost
questions.explain: Because each AZ has its own power, cooling, and network infrastructure, a failure in one AZ is isolated from the others, so spreading an application across multiple AZs protects it from a single-AZ outage.

questions.q: What is the difference between an IAM policy and an IAM role?
options: A policy and a role are interchangeable terms for the same IAM concept
A role defines permissions while a policy is an AWS employee who reviews access requests
A policy can only ever apply to S3 while a role applies to every other service
A policy is a JSON document that defines permissions; a role is an identity that can be assumed and has policies attached to it
questions.explain: A policy is a document describing what actions are allowed or denied on which resources, while a role is an identity (assumable by a user, service, or account) to which one or more policies are attached.

questions.q: What's a key architectural difference between EC2 and Lambda?
options: EC2 runs persistent virtual servers you provision and manage, while Lambda runs your code only in response to events without you provisioning servers
EC2 is serverless while Lambda requires you to manage the underlying servers
A single Lambda invocation can run continuously for multiple days
Once started, an EC2 instance can never be stopped or terminated
questions.explain: EC2 gives you a virtual machine that keeps running until you stop it, requiring you to manage the OS and capacity, whereas Lambda executes your code on demand in response to triggers and AWS manages the underlying compute.

questions.q: What's the fundamental difference between S3 and EBS?
options: S3 and EBS are simply two different names for the same underlying storage service
S3 is object storage accessed over the network via an API and isn't tied to any single server, while EBS is block storage attached to one EC2 instance at a time
EBS volumes have no size limit while S3 objects are capped at 5TB
S3 can only store plain text files while EBS can store any file type
questions.explain: S3 stores objects and is accessed over HTTP(S) from anywhere, independent of any compute instance, while EBS provides block storage volumes that attach to a single EC2 instance like a virtual hard drive.

questions.q: What is a VPC in AWS?
options: A physical firewall appliance that must be purchased and racked separately
A service that assigns your entire AWS account a single shared public IP address
A logically isolated virtual network within AWS where you control IP address ranges, subnets, and routing
A type of managed database used exclusively for user authentication
questions.explain: A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is a software-defined network you provision within AWS, where you define the IP address ranges, create subnets, and configure route tables and gateways to control connectivity.

questions.q: Which AWS EC2 pricing model offers the deepest discount in exchange for AWS being able to reclaim the instance at any time?
options: Spot Instances, because AWS can reclaim them with short notice in exchange for a steep discount off On-Demand pricing
On-Demand Instances, since there's no long-term commitment required
Reserved Instances, since they require a 1 or 3 year commitment
Dedicated Hosts, since you're renting an entire physical server
questions.explain: Spot Instances let you use spare EC2 capacity at up to a 90% discount versus On-Demand, but AWS can interrupt (reclaim) them with only a short warning when it needs that capacity for other customers.

questions.q: What does AWS Cost Explorer help you do?
options: Automatically reduce your bill without any configuration on your part
Grant IAM permissions in order to reduce your monthly cost
Replace the need for AWS Budgets and billing alerts entirely
Visualize, understand, and forecast your AWS spending over time
questions.explain: Cost Explorer is a reporting tool that lets you view historical spending patterns, break costs down by service or tag, and forecast future spend — it doesn't change your bill on its own.

questions.q: What is the recommended way to assign the same set of permissions to many IAM users?
options: Copy the same policy document individually onto every user
Add the users to an IAM group and attach the policy to the group instead of to each user
Give every user the AdministratorAccess managed policy
Share one IAM user's credentials among the whole team
questions.explain: IAM groups let you attach a policy once to the group and have it apply to every member, which is far easier to maintain than duplicating policies across individual users or sharing credentials.

questions.q: An IAM policy has both an explicit Deny statement and an Allow statement that would otherwise apply to the same action. What happens?
options: The explicit Deny always wins, regardless of any Allow statement elsewhere in the policy
The Allow always wins because IAM evaluates it last
IAM throws an error and blocks the entire policy from being attached
Whichever statement is listed first in the policy's JSON takes effect
questions.explain: IAM's evaluation logic is deny-by-default, and an explicit Deny in any applicable policy always overrides an Allow, regardless of where either statement appears or how many policies are involved.

questions.q: What does the principle of least privilege mean when designing IAM policies for a data pipeline?
options: Grant every role AdministratorAccess to avoid running into permission errors
Grant permissions based on whichever team requests access the fastest
Grant a role only the specific permissions it needs to do its job, and nothing more
Skip IAM roles entirely and rely on the account's root credentials
questions.explain: Least privilege means scoping each identity's permissions down to exactly what it needs to perform its function, minimizing the damage possible if credentials are ever leaked or misused.

questions.q: How does an AWS service like Lambda typically get permission to read from an S3 bucket on your behalf?
options: You must hardcode your personal IAM user's access keys into the Lambda function's code
Lambda automatically has read/write access to every S3 bucket in the account by default
You email AWS Support to manually request cross-service access on your behalf
You attach an IAM execution role to the Lambda function that grants it the specific S3 permissions it needs
questions.explain: Lambda functions run under an IAM execution role, and that role's attached policies determine exactly which actions the function can perform against other services like S3 — nothing is granted automatically.

questions.q: What is the AWS CLI primarily used for?
options: Interacting with AWS services from a terminal using scriptable, automatable text commands
A graphical drag-and-drop tool for designing architecture diagrams
A monitoring dashboard limited to billing alerts
A visual replacement for IAM that manages permissions without policies
questions.explain: The AWS CLI is a command-line tool that lets you call any supported AWS API from a terminal, which makes it well suited to scripting and automating tasks that would otherwise require the console.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using an AWS SDK, like Boto3 for Python, instead of the CLI when building an application?
options: SDKs are the only supported way to authenticate to AWS
It lets your application call AWS services programmatically from within your own code, instead of shelling out to run CLI commands
SDKs are free to use while the CLI requires a paid subscription
Using an SDK removes the need for IAM credentials entirely
questions.explain: An SDK provides native language bindings so your application code can call AWS APIs directly, handling things like request signing and retries internally, rather than spawning a separate CLI process.

questions.q: When you deploy your first resource in AWS, such as launching an EC2 instance, which of these is required beforehand for the resource to have network connectivity?
options: A Redshift cluster running in the same account
A CloudFront distribution pointed at the instance
A VPC, and typically a subnet within it, for the instance to launch into
An AWS Organizations account with member accounts configured
questions.explain: Every EC2 instance launches into a VPC subnet, which determines its network configuration; without a VPC and subnet in place, the instance has nowhere to attach a network interface.

questions.q: Where do certifications like AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner and AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate sit relative to each other?
options: They test the exact same content at the exact same difficulty level
Solutions Architect Associate must be earned before Cloud Practitioner is available
Cloud Practitioner is reserved for people who already hold a Professional-level certification
Cloud Practitioner is a foundational-level cert testing broad awareness, while Solutions Architect Associate is an associate-level cert testing deeper hands-on architecture knowledge
questions.explain: AWS certifications are tiered: Foundational (Cloud Practitioner) covers broad, high-level awareness, while Associate-level certs like Solutions Architect Associate go deeper into hands-on design and implementation knowledge.
